title: Towards Fairness Assessment of Dutch Hate Speech Detection
findings: Fine-tuning hate speech models with counterfactual data generally improved fairness for non-toxic sentences containing religious terms. However, for toxic sentences, the counterfactual fairness for the religion category was often worse in the fine-tuned models compared to the baseline model, indicating that the debiasing methods did not consistently improve fairness for toxic religious content.

measurement_description: Fairness (Counterfactual Token Fairness and Group Fairness) of hate speech detection models with respect to religious identity terms. The evaluation measures how model predictions change when religious identity terms are substituted in text.
